text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton urged the IRA on Thursday to "lay down their guns for good" in order to bring a lasting peace to Northern Ireland.

Clinton told a news conference during a one-day trip to Britain that efforts to resolve the province's future could only succeed "if there's an unequivocal ceasefire, in deed and in word. Again, I urge the IRA (Irish Republican Army) to lay down their guns for good."

The United States has been a key player in long-running efforts to bring a lasting peace to Northern Ireland and Clinton has repeatedly called on the IRA, a guerrilla group fighting to end British rule of the province, to call a ceasefire.
He welcomed initiatives by the new British government to kick-start the logjammed peace process and said the Americans would be there to help out.

"We have a new British government that has taken what are, I think, wise and judicious steps and made statements that I think are clear, unequivocal and appropriate," Clinton said in a joint news conference with British Prime Minister Tony Blair.
Clinton said it was up to the parties involved to bring about a settlement, adding: "We'll be there, active and involved, along the way."
